title: Financial intelligence: your money journey
summary: Six steps to take control of your money: where you are, where you're going, and how to get there.

lessons.title: What financial intelligence means
points: Financial intelligence is not about how much you earn. It is about the daily habit of controlling spending, living below your means, choosing needs over wants, and keeping part…
lessons.key_idea: Without this discipline, saving stays weak and financial freedom stays out of reach — no matter how big the income.

lessons.title: The six steps of the journey
points: 1. Know where you are — your income, expenses, what you own and what you owe.
2. Choose your destination — goals for your business, family, home and future.
3. Find the gap — the difference between where you are and where you want to be.
4. Plan the route — earn more, cut expenses, save regularly.
5. Watch for risks — job loss, sickness, price increases.
lessons.key_idea: Talk about money with the people close to you. A family that plans together reaches the destination together.

title: The pie: pay yourself first
summary: Split every income into Living, Savings and Give — and choose your tier: Seed, Grow or Harvest.

lessons.title: Turn the formula around
points: Most people do this: Income − Expenses = whatever is left to save. Usually nothing is left.

lessons.title: Your three slices
points: Living — food, rent, transport, bills, daily spending. Practise contentment here.
Savings — your future: emergency fund, goals, long-term savings.
Give & Family — family support, religious giving, helping your community.
lessons.key_idea: Whatever is left of your Give share at the end of the period moves into your emergency fund. On Harvest, that can take your savings to 50%.

title: The snowball: get rich slowly
summary: Small savings, kept up for years, grow into real wealth. Why ₦10 a day beats ₦1 a day by far more than 10×.

lessons.title: Two people, same income
points: Trader A spends ₦9,900 and saves ₦100 a day → ₦10,000 after 100 days.
Trader B spends ₦9,000 and saves ₦1,000 a day → ₦100,000 after 100 days.
lessons.key_idea: Earning more will not make you wealthy if you keep spending it all.

lessons.title: Why the snowball grows faster over time
points: Savings that earn interest grow, and the interest earns interest too. This is compounding. Over many years it turns steady saving into a large sum.
lessons.key_idea: Beware of 'get rich quick'. Wealth is built slowly, by saving regularly for a long time.

title: Cut costs, cut back, cut out
summary: Three simple ways to reduce what you spend without making life miserable.

lessons.title: The three cuts
points: Cut costs — do the same thing, cheaper. Buy foodstuff in bulk at the market instead of daily.
Cut back — do it less often. Eat out twice a week instead of five times.
Cut out — stop it completely. Cancel the subscription you never use.

lessons.title: Don't spend what you saved
points: When you cut an expense, the money must go somewhere useful — or it quietly disappears into other spending. Move what you cut straight into savings.
lessons.key_idea: Need or want? Before each purchase, ask: do I need this, or do I just want it?

title: Budgeting, tracking, or a system?
summary: Three ways to control expenses, and when each one works best.

lessons.title: Track first, budget later
points: Budget — plan ahead. Best when life is changing (new job, marriage, moving).
Tracking — see what really happens. Best when spending feels out of control.
A system — split income automatically. Best for building savings for years.

lessons.title: Make it realistic
points: Keep a 10% buffer for unexpected costs.
Allow a little fun and gifts — a budget that's too strict breaks.
Aim to save at least 20% of your income.
Involve your partner or family.
lessons.key_idea: Kopkad logs your Kopkad wallet and savings transactions for you, so tracking takes less effort.

title: Your emergency fund
summary: From a small cash buffer to six months of living costs — your protection when life happens.

lessons.title: Why you need one
points: Sickness, a slow market, a broken phone, a rent increase — emergencies come without warning. Without savings, people borrow at high cost or sell what they own.

lessons.title: How big, and where
points: Step 1: never let your spending money run to zero — keep a small buffer.
Step 2: save one month of living costs.
Step 3: grow it to three, then six months.
lessons.key_idea: Your unspent Give share moves into your emergency fund first.

title: Good debt vs bad debt
summary: When borrowing builds wealth, and when it quietly destroys it.

lessons.title: Bad debt
points: Borrowing to pay for daily expenses or celebrations.
Buy-now-pay-later that you can't clear quickly.
Loans for things that lose value, like phones and cars.
Borrowing to gamble or chase quick profits.

lessons.title: Good debt
points: Good debt helps you buy something that grows in value or brings in more money than the loan costs — for example, stock for your shop that you are sure will sell at a profit.
lessons.key_idea: Before you borrow, ask: will this bring in more than it costs me, and can I repay even if business is slow?

title: Your three money statements
summary: What you own, what you earn, and where your cash goes — explained simply.

lessons.title: Balance sheet and income statement
points: Balance sheet: what you own − what you owe = your net worth. A snapshot on one day.
Income statement: income − expenses = your profit (what you saved) over a month.

lessons.title: Cash flow is different
points: Cash flow tracks actual money moving in and out. A loan brings cash in, but it is not income — you owe it back. Repaying a loan sends cash out, but it is not an expense.
lessons.key_idea: Treating borrowed money as income is how many people overspend.

title: Fixed vs variable costs
summary: Why high fixed costs make you fragile when income drops.

lessons.title: Two kinds of expense
points: Fixed — the same every month whatever you earn: rent, school fees, loan repayments.
Variable — changes with your choices: food out, transport, data, clothes.

lessons.title: Stay flexible
points: Before taking on a new fixed cost — a bigger flat, a car loan — ask whether you could still pay it in your worst month. Mark each expense as fixed or variable in Wealth Builder…
lessons.key_idea: Lower fixed costs plus an emergency fund = less fear when business slows down.

title: Financial independence: your number
summary: The point where your savings can pay your living costs — and how to estimate it.

lessons.title: Independence, not just being rich
points: Financial independence means your savings and investments earn enough to cover your living costs, so work becomes a choice. It is not about flashy cars or houses — those often…

lessons.title: Estimate your number
points: A common rule of thumb: multiply your yearly living costs by 30.
lessons.key_idea: For educational purposes only. This is not financial advice.

title: Investing basics: risk and time
summary: The main types of assets, how risky they are, and how long to hold them. Education only.

lessons.title: Types of assets
points: Cash and savings — low risk, low return, easy to reach. For money you need within a year.
Fixed-income (treasury bills, bonds) — a little more return, money tied up for a period. For one to five years.
Property — can grow over many years but costly to buy and slow to sell. Five years or more.
Shares (e.g. companies on the Nigerian Exchange) — can grow and pay dividends, but prices rise and fall. Five years or more.
lessons.key_idea: For educational purposes only. This is not financial advice. Kopkad does not offer investment products; Locked Savings is a savings product.

lessons.title: Risk, time and spreading out
points: Higher possible return comes with higher risk of loss.
Only put money in long-term assets if you won't need it for years.
Don't put everything in one place — spread it out (diversify).
Build your emergency fund first.
Your skills are your biggest asset — investing in learning raises your income.
lessons.key_idea: Speak to a licensed professional before making investment decisions.

title: Avoiding scams and speculation
summary: How to spot 'double your money' schemes and why speculation is closer to gambling than investing.

lessons.title: Red flags
points: Guaranteed high returns in a short time ('double your money in 30 days').
Pressure to pay quickly or recruit friends and family.
No clear business that produces the returns.
Withdrawals that keep getting delayed.
lessons.key_idea: For educational purposes only. This is not financial advice.

lessons.title: Speculation is not investing
points: Short-term trading of crypto, forex or 'signals', and contracts for difference, depend on prices moving the right way in a short time. Most people who try it lose money. The…
lessons.key_idea: Get rich slowly: steady saving over many years beats chasing quick wins.

title: The seven cures for a thin wallet
summary: Timeless rules from a 100-year-old classic: keep part of every income, control spending, and make money work.

lessons.title: Keep part of everything you earn
points: A famous story set in ancient Babylon asks: why do hard-working people stay broke? The answer it gives is simple — they spend everything that comes in. The first cure is to keep…

lessons.title: Make money work, and protect it
points: Make your savings earn — money sitting idle loses value.
Guard it from loss — never chase promises that sound too good.
Own your home in time — rent paid forever never comes back.
Plan for the day you can't work — an emergency fund and insurance.
Grow your ability to earn — a new skill is the best raise.
lessons.key_idea: Save first, spend what's left, protect what you save, and keep learning.

title: Assets put money in your pocket
summary: The simple test that separates things that make you richer from things that quietly make you poorer.

lessons.title: The pocket test
points: Asset: savings that earn interest, a shop or tricycle that earns more than it costs to run, a skill people pay you for.
Liability: a car you only use to show off, a phone bought on credit, a loan for a party.

lessons.title: Buy assets first, enjoy later
points: Robert T. Kiyosaki, Rich Dad Poor Dad (1997) — assets vs liabilities. Some of the book's other claims are debated; the pocket test is the…
lessons.key_idea: Before a big purchase, ask: will this put money in my pocket, or take it out every month?

title: Money is about behaviour, not cleverness
summary: Why doing ordinary things consistently beats being smart — and why knowing 'enough' protects you.

lessons.title: Behaviour beats knowledge
points: Your past shapes your money habits — what feels 'normal' to you may not be normal for others.
Luck and risk both play a part — don't copy a lucky winner, and don't judge yourself by one bad year.
Compounding needs time more than it needs high returns.

lessons.title: Know your 'enough' and leave room for error
points: Morgan Housel, The Psychology of Money (2020) — behaviour over knowledge, 'enough', luck and risk, room for error.
lessons.key_idea: Getting rich and staying rich are different skills. Staying rich means not taking risks you can't survive.

title: Being rich vs looking rich
summary: Most people who build real wealth live quietly below their means. Here's how to handle the pressure to show off.

lessons.title: Wealth is what you don't see
points: A long-running study of self-made millionaires found that most of them live well below their means: ordinary houses, ordinary cars, and a habit of saving the difference. The…
lessons.key_idea: Wealth is the money you didn't spend. You can't see it — that's the point.

lessons.title: Owambe, aso-ebi and the pressure to spend
points: Put celebrations in your Give & Family share, not in borrowed money.
Set a yearly aso-ebi and gifts budget and stick to it.
Say 'not this time' to one event a month — that's a cut you can save.
Spend on what you value, not on what others will see.

title: Clearing debt: snowball or avalanche
summary: Two proven ways to pay off several debts — pick the one you'll actually stick with.

lessons.title: List every debt
points: Write down every debt: who you owe, how much, the interest or fees, and the minimum payment. Include loan apps, buy-now-pay-later, money owed to family and the shop credit you…
lessons.key_idea: Stop adding new debt while you clear the old — otherwise you're filling a bucket with a hole.

lessons.title: Two ways to pay it down
points: Snowball — the smallest balance first. Clearing one quickly feels good and keeps you going; its payment then rolls onto the next.
Avalanche — the highest interest first. It costs the least in total, but the first win can take longer.

title: Inflation and the Rule of 72
summary: Why cash kept at home shrinks, and a quick trick to see how fast money doubles — or halves.

lessons.title: Inflation eats idle money
points: Inflation is prices rising over time. If prices go up 15% in a year, ₦10,000 kept under the mattress buys only what about ₦8,700 bought a year ago.
lessons.key_idea: Keep only what you need for the next few weeks as idle cash. Savings that earn something fight back against inflation.

lessons.title: The Rule of 72
points: At 12% a year, savings double in about 72 ÷ 12 = 6 years.
At 15% inflation, idle cash loses half its buying power in about 72 ÷ 15 ≈ 5 years.
lessons.key_idea: For educational purposes only. This is not financial advice.

title: Make saving automatic
summary: Willpower runs out. Set things up once so saving happens before you can spend.

lessons.title: Don't rely on willpower
points: Fixed costs — rent, bills, school fees.
Savings and long-term money — taken out first.
Guilt-free spending — whatever remains is yours to enjoy without worry.
lessons.key_idea: When your savings are already set aside, the rest of your money is truly free to spend.

lessons.title: Automating it in Kopkad
points: Ramit Sethi, I Will Teach You to Be Rich (2009) — the 'conscious spending plan' and automating your money.

title: What does it really cost? Count it in hours
summary: Turn prices into hours of your life — the quickest way to tell a need from a want.

lessons.title: Your real hourly earning
points: Every naira you spend cost you time to earn. Work out what you really earn per hour: take what you keep in a week and divide by all the hours work takes — including travel and…

lessons.title: Is it worth the hours?
points: Vicki Robin & Joe Dominguez, Your Money or Your Life (1992) — money as 'life energy' and your real hourly wage.
lessons.key_idea: Spend your life energy on what you truly value.

title: Spotting Ponzi schemes: lessons from CBEX
summary: How 'double your money' schemes work, why they collapse, and how to check a company before you invest.

lessons.title: How a Ponzi scheme works
points: A Ponzi scheme pays early members with money from new members, not from real profit. It works only while new money keeps coming in — when it slows, withdrawals stop and most…
lessons.key_idea: For educational purposes only. This is not financial advice.

lessons.title: Check before you invest
points: Guaranteed high returns in days or weeks — no real business can promise that.
You must recruit people to earn or to withdraw.
Withdrawals that get delayed, capped or 'upgraded'.
A big name or 'AI' and 'crypto' words, but no clear way the money is made.
lessons.key_idea: Under the Investments and Securities Act 2025, Ponzi promoters can face up to 10 years in prison. If it sounds too good to be true, it is.
